overall.summary: The customer-service-calls part is said to barely matter in Oregon, where the calls count most; one evidence sentence of the heavy daytime use part cites the wrong claim. The rest reproduces.

findings.statement: for customers in Oregon the calls barely matter
findings.check: probe --sweep 'number customer service calls=0:6:7' --sweep state=49,37; claim C093
findings.evidence: Oregon: part contribution -1.964 at 0 calls, -0.712 at 1, +0.540 at 2, +1.791 at 3 (risk 0.5% -> 17.6%); West Virginia: +0.99 -> +1.79 (2.5% -> 5.4%). C093: calls are amplified in Oregon (effect 3.76 logits vs 0.80 elsewhere). The calls matter more in Oregon, not less; the part's own evidence sentence says so.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ced675 --sweep "number customer service calls=0:6:7" --sweep state=49,37

findings.statement: It acts on 747 of 4000 training customers, 269 of whom left; ... about 5% without it and about 23% with it. [C086]
findings.evidence: 269, 5% and 23% are not in C086 (the day-minutes threshold claim); they are in C088 (subgroup:active, 747 active, 269 positives, risk 0.049 -> 0.225), which is the claim that should be cited.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify recheck experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ced675

findings.statement: coverage 1.0, full, hierarchy complete, preservation 5.6e-16, closed-form error 0.028
mean-ablation per child: backbone -0.084, csc -0.079, day/eve hinge -0.038, states -0.003
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify ablate experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ced675 --part ann_81 --to mean

findings.statement: flat logit for 0-2 calls, then about +1.25 per call; state 37 switches 1255 off
findings.evidence: WV contribution 0.99, 1.06, 1.13 for 0-2 calls, then 1.79, 3.04, 4.30, 5.55 (+1.25 per call); in Oregon linear throughout
